chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me who said: Abu Sa'id al-Adamy narrated to us who said: Al-Hasan ibn al-Hussein al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sin'an, from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Indeed, a group of people from the Quraysh had little moderation in their dealings with the people, so they were expelled from the Quraysh. And by God, whatever there is in their records is suffering. And indeed, a group of others had good moderation in their dealings, so they joined the lofty household. He said: Then said: Whoever withdraws his hand from the people, he only withdraws one hand from them, but many hands will be withdrawn from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of moderation in social dealings according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the Shia principle that social merit (mudarat) outweighs tribal lineage, illustrating how Quraysh were expelled despite their nobility due to poor social conduct, while others were integrated through good manners. The Imam’s concluding maxim on reciprocity underscores the practical wisdom of maintaining social bonds, reflecting the broader ethical framework in al-Khisal where character determines one's standing in the community.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-60 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar quoted on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Adamy, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Hussein al-Lu’lu’ee, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sin’an that Hazifat ibn Mansoor said that he had heard Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) say,

“A group of people from the Quraysh tribe reduced their (level of) treatment of the people with moderation, and were thrown out of the Quraysh tribe. And by God, whatever there is in their records is suffering. Another group of people from the Quraysh tribe treated the people with moderation and joined the lofty household (of the Prophet).” Then he added, “Whoever withdraws his hand from the people has withdrawn just one hand, but many hands will be withdrawn from him.”
